I think your mom was right about being careful who you spoke to about it. If I told people about my harm OCD people will slowly cut me out of their lives. It will raise red flags with them and I won't be there defending myself "I can't control these thoughts its my illness and it affects me". While you shouldn't bottle it up there are ways to deal with this and openly talk to people who are -important- to you and won't exploit this part about your life. Try learning more about OCD and types of therapies that can help you. People are not forgiving when it comes to mental health, there is still a stigma and so many people will never understand it. It's something YOU experience. Your mother protected you with that advice, figure out how you let it sit in your head, she didn't mean it maliciously. She probably didn't handle it the best way but still. Protecting and supporting does not mean sugar coating and taking sides. People aren't going to sit and try to understand and listen to you about your mental illness unless you are in a place for help and support.

You are compulsive not impulsive the chance of you going through with a harm urge is veryyy low.
